title: IDP-only sources are handed a combined-pool percentile but scored on the IDP-slice Hill master, so they vote ~48% of the anchor's value at the identical effective rank
subsystem: Core value blend — scope curve routing
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md step 3/5: 'Scope-appropriate curve routing (cross-market -> GLOBAL, overall IDP -> IDP, everything else -> OFFENSE)'; the dlfIdp registry entry says shared-market ladder translation 'correctly calibrates DLF against the retail offense market'. Both together assert every source's contribution lands in one 0-9999 coordinate system.
observed: `needs_shared_market_translation` rewrites an IDP-only source's rank into COMBINED-pool coordinates (dlfIdp/idpShow/fantasyProsIdp raw rank 1 -> effective rank 34 for Aidan Hutchinson, the same slot idpTradeCalc gives him). `_percentile_denom_for_source` then divides by 500 (combined-pool N) and `_curve_for_source` routes by SCOPE to the IDP master (c=0.0830) which was fit on IDPTradeCalc's IDP-only slice. The two coordinate systems are inconsistent: at percentile 0.0661 the IDP master pays 5627 while the value-direct anchor on the same row pays 6444. Measured over the whole board the four IDP-scope rank-signal sources contribute a median 0.461/0.474/0.481/0.485 of idpTradeCalc's contribution on the same row. On offense — where source rank space and curve space agree — every source clusters at 0.87-1.08 of the anchor. Re-scoring the SAME percentiles through the GLOBAL master (the curve fit on the combined pool the ladder maps into) returns median ratios 0.92/1.32/1.29/0.95.

reproduction.expected: IDP-scope source contribution / idpTradeCalc contribution ~= 1.0 on the same row (as offense achieves)

numericProof.formula: V(p) = 9999 / (1 + (p/c)^s) evaluated at the SAME p for the IDP master vs the GLOBAL master

userImpact: Every IDP row's 'multi-source consensus' is dragged down by a units error rather than by disagreement: three sources that rank Aidan Hutchinson their #1 IDP are shown, in the /rankings value-chain panel, as valuing him 13% below the one source that ranks him 34th. A user reads real disagreement where the sources actually agree exactly, and sells IDP assets into a board biased low.

priorFinding.note: Prior said '~48% of the IDP market at the same rank'. Independently measured 46.1-48.5% median over 605 source votes on the 2026-08-04 board, plus the GLOBAL-curve counterfactual that isolates the mechanism.

whatWorks: The shared-market ladder translation itself is correct — it lands IDP rank 1 on exactly the combined-pool rank the anchor gives. Only the curve chosen afterwards is wrong.
rootCause: `_curve_for_source` routes on `scope`, while `_percentile_denom_for_source` and the ladder both operate in combined-pool space. Scope is the wrong key: what determines the right curve is which POOL the effective rank lives in, and after `needs_shared_market_translation` that pool is the combined one.
requiredRepair: Route any source whose effective rank has been ladder-translated into combined-pool space through the GLOBAL master (or, equivalently, key `_curve_for_source` on `sharedMarketTranslated`/`needs_rookie_translation` rather than on `scope`). Re-fit is not required — the GLOBAL master is already the combined-pool curve.
dependencies: Fixing this changes 52 anchor ejections (W02-F002) and most of the 127 corridor clamps (W02-F003); those two findings should be re-measured after, not fixed independently.

title: The Hampel filter ejects the designated IDP market anchor on 29.4% of Hampel-eligible IDP rows, and in 52 of 52 cases for being HIGH
subsystem: Core value blend — per-player outlier rejection
claimUnderTest: `_hampel_filter_per_player` docstring: 'catches the "FootballGuys is way off on this one player" case without dropping the whole source globally'. The registry calls idpTradeCalc 'the retail IDP authority and the backbone source'.
observed: On the live board `idpTradeCalc` is Hampel-dropped on 52 IDP rows — 29.4% of the 177 IDP rows that carry >= 4 sources (17.7% of all 293 ranked IDP rows). Direction is not random: in 52/52 cases the anchor was ejected for sitting ABOVE the median of its peers. That is the exact signature of W02-F001 — the peers are on a ~2x compressed scale, so the correctly-scaled market anchor is the statistical outlier. Named victims include Maxx Crosby, T.J. Watt, Micah Parsons (via the same mechanism), Jalen Carter, Kyle Hamilton, Roquan Smith and Trey Hendrickson. Board-wide the filter drops 192 of 6,442 source votes (2.98%) across 168 of 800 rows (21.0%).

priorFinding.note: Prior reported 28%. Reproduced at 29.4% of Hampel-eligible IDP rows on the 2026-08-04 board; the 28% figure only reconciles against that denominator (it is 17.7% of all ranked IDP rows). Direction (52/52 high) is a new measurement.

whatWorks: The Hampel implementation itself is exactly correct — an independent reimplementation reproduced the `droppedSources` stamp on 800/800 rows with zero mismatches.
rootCause: Downstream symptom of W02-F001: the reference median is computed across sources that are not on a common scale.
requiredRepair: Fix W02-F001 first, then re-measure. If a residual remains, exclude designated anchor sources from being ejection CANDIDATES (they may still set the median) — a filter whose job is to remove a rogue source must not be able to remove the reference price.

title: The corridor clamp's per-bucket P90 machinery is inert — the 0.15 cap binds on 100% of clamps — and it rewrites 43.3% of ranked IDP rows to exactly idpTradeCalc x 0.85 or x 1.15
subsystem: Core value blend — market corridor clamp
claimUnderTest: `_apply_market_corridor_clamp` docstring: 'Band width is empirical — P90 of |final - market| / market computed within each confidence bucket'; the Phase-4c call site: 'Leaves 90% of the board untouched — only the tail outliers ... get pulled back to the band edge.' CLAUDE.md step 10: 'P90 drift band per confidence bucket, hard band cap 0.15'.
observed: Measured on the live board the per-bucket P90 drifts are 0.4805 (medium, n=91), 0.5097 (low, n=173) and 0.5228 (high, n=29) — every one of them 3x the 0.15 asset-class cap. `cappedByMaxBand` is therefore true on 127 of 127 clamped rows: the percentile computation, the per-bucket split, the `_MARKET_CORRIDOR_MIN_BUCKET_N` fallback and the `_MARKET_CORRIDOR_PERCENTILE` constant are all dead weight, and the live behaviour is a flat +/-15% band around one source. It does not leave 90% untouched: 127 of the 293 eligible rows (43.3%) are rewritten, mean move 464.7 points (28.9% of the pre-clamp value), max 110.9% (a value more than doubled). On all 127 the published `rankDerivedValue` equals `round(marketAnchor * (1 +/- 0.15))` to within 1 — i.e. the number a user sees is a pure function of a single source, with the other four contributing nothing. 126 of 127 anchor on `idpTradeCalc`; 1 anchors on `fantasyProsIdp` via the stage-2 fallback chain.

reproduction.actual: 127/127 capped at 0.15; 43.3% of eligible rows clamped; 127/127 land exactly on anchor*(1+/-0.15)

userImpact: On /rankings and in every trade engine, 127 IDP players carry a value that is arithmetically 0.85x or 1.15x one vendor's number. Nothing on the page says so — `marketCorridorClamp` is materialised onto the row by `buildRows` (frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1070) and rendered by no component. A user comparing our board to IDPTradeCalc believes they are seeing independent corroboration; they are seeing the same number scaled by a constant.

priorFinding.note: Prior said the cap binds on 100% of clamps. Reproduced (127/127) and extended with the clamp RATE (43.3% of eligible, against a docstring claiming 90% untouched), the magnitude distribution (mean 28.9%, max 110.9%), and the exactness proof that all 127 published values equal anchor*(1+/-0.15).

whatWorks: The clamp is correctly scoped: 0 offense rows and 0 pick rows were clamped, matching CLAUDE.md's 'IDP rows only'. The `marketCorridorClamp` stamp is complete and honest in the payload.
rootCause: Two independent bands were layered without checking whether the empirical one ever wins. It never does, because the drift distribution the P90 is measured over is itself inflated by W02-F001.
requiredRepair: Either delete the P90/bucket machinery and document the band as a flat +/-15% policy, or fix W02-F001 (which should collapse the drift distribution) and re-measure whether a clamp is still needed at all. Whichever is chosen, surface the clamp on the row — a value that is a constant times one vendor's price must not render identically to a genuine 14-source blend.

title: The blend is not monotone in a source's own vote: raising idpTradeCalc's contribution by 3% drops the pre-clamp blended value 25.8%
claimUnderTest: Implicit and load-bearing everywhere downstream: a better source rank / higher source value produces a higher blended value. The count-aware mean-median blend and the alpha-shrinkage combine are both monotone by construction, which is what makes the property look guaranteed.
observed: Holding Dallas Turner's four other source contributions fixed and sweeping idpTradeCalc's contribution, the pre-clamp blended value rises smoothly to 2502.3 at 3300, then falls to 1856.6 at 3400 — a 25.8% drop caused by a 3.0% INCREASE in one input, because the Hampel threshold crosses and the anchor is ejected. Above 3400 the blend is completely insensitive to the anchor (flat 1856.6 out to 5200). The composed post-clamp value happens to stay monotone on this row only because the clamp re-derives it from the ejected source; the blend itself — the number stamped as `_blendedValueUncapped` and used to price every unranked rookie and therefore every current-year pick via tethering — is discontinuous. Every other stage verified monotone: per-source `valueContribution` is strictly decreasing in effective rank with 0 inversions across all 21 sources once TE rows (where the premium deliberately repositions within the scale) are excluded.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/full.json; python3 docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W02/repro_blend.py ; see docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W02/dallas-turner-sweep.json
reproduction.expected: blended value non-decreasing in each source's contribution

userImpact: A source revising a player UPWARD can move our board DOWN. Because `_blendedValueUncapped` is what the rookie pool is sorted by, a discontinuity there also reorders which rookie a current-year pick tethers to, so the instability propagates to the pick board.

priorFinding.note: The prior audit reported the anchor-ejection rate (A11-F01) but not that the ejection makes the blend a non-monotone function of its own inputs, nor that the blend is flat in the anchor above the ejection threshold.

whatWorks: Every deterministic stage (Hill curve, count-aware blend, alpha-shrinkage, single-source haircut, clamp) is individually monotone; only the Hampel gate breaks it.
rootCause: Hard-thresholded outlier rejection composed with an aggregator makes the composition a step function of every input.
requiredRepair: Replace the hard drop with a continuous down-weight (e.g. Huber/Tukey weights on the same deviation statistic) so a source's influence tapers rather than vanishing at a threshold.

title: Ranks past the fixed 500-row reference collapse to one value: 440 rank-signal votes carry zero ordering information, including 164 of idpShow's 279
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md step 2: 'Percentile normalization against a FIXED 500-rank combined-pool reference (ranks past 500 clamp to the curve tail; this is deliberate top-500-board behavior)'.
observed: `percentile_to_value` clamps p to [0,1], so every effective rank >= 500 evaluates at p=1.0 and returns the identical tail value. 743 of 6,442 source votes (11.5%) sit at p=1.0; 440 of those are on the rank->Hill path where the clamp actually destroys information. The effect is concentrated on IDP because the shared-market ladder pushes IDP ordinals deep into combined space: idpShow's raw ranks 146 through 344 — 199 distinct ordinal positions — all contribute exactly 594; fantasyProsIdp 146-211 and dlfIdp 146-170 likewise contribute 594; draftSharksIdp's raw ranks 100-315 all contribute exactly 1698. Those sources' entire deep board is a constant. The board's own minimum ranked value is 757, so the constant sits below everything the board publishes. 'Deliberate top-500-board behavior' is a fair description for offense (5.5% of draftSharks' votes clamp) but not for IDP, where 59-64% of a source's votes are collapsed.

whatWorks: On offense the clamp is genuinely marginal — 21 of draftSharks' 381 votes, 0 for every other offense source.

dependencies: W02-F001 shares the same root confusion about which pool a translated rank lives in.

title: Three publishers get two equal votes each in the blend; the registry's own correlation groups are never applied to weighting
claimUnderTest: Registry comment on ktcSfTep: 'fantasyNavigatorSf republishes KTC-derived numbers, so the two are not independent votes and must leave the blend together'. CLAUDE.md: 'Blend weights live in the _RANKING_SOURCES registry (all 1.0 by policy)' — i.e. one equal vote per source.
observed: `correlation_group` is read in exactly two places — the `/api/rankings/sources` stamp and `expand_correlation_groups`, which is used only to co-exclude sources when a caller drops one. It never reaches `blend_weight_by_source`. On the live board ktcSfTep and fantasyNavigatorSf (whose rows carry `ktc_player_id`) both vote at weight 1.0 on 368 rows; fantasyProsSf and fantasyProsFitzmaurice both vote on 298 rows; dlfSf and dlfRookieSf both vote on 33 rookie rows; dlfIdp and dlfRookieIdp on 12. On a typical 14-vote offense row that is 2 of 14 votes for KTC and 2 of 14 for FantasyPros — 28.6% of the consensus from two publishers.

reproduction.expected: correlated publishers share one vote's worth of weight, or the registry documents that they do not
reproduction.actual: 368 / 298 / 33 / 12 rows with two full-weight votes from one publisher

userImpact: The board is more KTC-shaped than the 'multi-source consensus' framing implies, and a user who disables KTC on /settings expecting an independent board still gets its republisher unless the correlation-group expansion path is exercised.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with per-pair row counts and the code trace showing correlation_group reaches only expand_correlation_groups, never the blend weights.

whatWorks: `expand_correlation_groups` does work for its stated purpose — excluding ktcSfTep also excludes fantasyNavigatorSf.
rootCause: Correlation was modelled as an exclusion property, not a weighting property.
requiredRepair: Divide the declared weight of each member of a correlation group by the number of that group's members actually voting on the row, before the count-aware blend. Keep the trim observation-based so equal-weight parity is preserved when no group has 2+ voters.

title: Every tunable in the blend was chosen against a stability metric the reports themselves say rewards ignoring 15 of 16 sources, and the one recommendation those reports make was not applied
claimUnderTest: The constants block presents alpha=0.10, lambda=0.0 and N=500 as backtested choices.
observed: `reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md` states its own metric is 'value-weighted rank change (lower = more stable)' and carries the caveat 'this metric rewards stability. The stability optimum drifts toward alpha=0 and lambda=0 — use the anchor source alone, ignore the 15 other sources.' The chosen alpha=0.10 is therefore a hand-picked compromise, not a measured optimum, and no report in `reports/` scores the live board against realized outcomes. `reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md` explicitly recommends 'Promote N=400 (+2.01% vs N=500 on the value-weighted metric)'; the live `_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N` is 500. So the constants are simultaneously justified by these reports and not governed by them.

reproduction.expected: the promoted constant matches the report's recommendation, or a decision record explains the divergence
reproduction.actual: report says promote N=400; code ships N=500; no ADR cited at the constant

userImpact: Every number on the platform inherits constants tuned to minimise day-to-day movement rather than to be right; a board optimised for stability will systematically under-react to real market moves, which is the opposite of what a dynasty trader needs.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced from the report files themselves, plus the new observation that percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md's own recommendation (N=400) was never applied.

whatWorks: The reports exist, are checked in, state their metric plainly, and flag their own degenerate optimum — the provenance is honest, only the validation target is wrong.
rootCause: No accuracy target was ever defined for the live board; `docs/architecture/optimization-target.md` names 'market consensus fit', which is a stability-adjacent target, not an outcome one.

title: `derived = int(norm_val)` truncates where every neighbouring stamp rounds, publishing a value 1 point below the blend on 280 rows

title: Missing data abstains rather than defaulting: the only fabricated values on the board are the 12 synthetic 2029 picks, and their provenance is disclosed in the payload and rendered
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: soft fallbacks are diagnostics-only and never touch the math; missing data is never imputed into a normal-looking value.
observed: 280 of 1,092 rows publish `rankDerivedValue: null` rather than a floor value. The soft-fallback count is stamped but provably unused (the clean-room reimplementation using covered sources only matches on 800/800 rows). The value-direct branch's fallback to the Hill curve only fires for a source that DID rank the player, so it is not imputation. The one genuine fabrication is `_inject_far_future_pick_sources`: 12 '2029 ...' rows are verbatim clones of the 2028 rows' per-source values (2029 Early 1st carries idpTradeCalc 5034, identical to 2028 Early 1st) multiplied by 0.53. Those rows are ranked and visible (2029 Early 1st at rank 207, value 2668). They are, however, honestly labelled: `confidenceLabel: 'Low — single pick source'`, `isSingleSource: true`, and `sourceAudit.allowlistReason` reads 'synthetic_far_future_tier: no vendor prices picks this far out; cloned from the nearest published year and year-discounted' — which `board-sections.jsx:233` renders. Side-effect worth noting: the clone loses `ktcSfTep` (present on 2028, absent on 2029), so the only surviving vote is idpTradeCalc.
